metadata.description: Evaluation criteria and scoring rubric for Clean Architecture compliance assessment
metadata.based_on: Clean Architecture by Robert C. Martin (2017)

principles.dependency_rule: Source code dependencies can only point inward. Nothing in an inner circle can know anything at all about something in an outer circle.

layers.name: Entities
layers.description: Enterprise-wide business rules. These are the most stable and reusable objects. They encapsulate the critical business data and logic.
indicators: Plain objects (POJOs/POPOs/POCOs) with no framework dependencies
Contain enterprise business rules that would exist even without the application
Can be used across multiple applications

layers.name: Use Cases
layers.description: Application-specific business rules. These orchestrate the flow of data to and from entities.
indicators: Named after business operations (e.g., PlaceOrder, RegisterCustomer)
Depend only on entities and abstract interfaces
Framework-independent; no HTTP, database, or UI knowledge

layers.name: Interface Adapters
layers.description: Convert data from the format most convenient for use cases to the format most convenient for external agencies (DB, Web, etc.).
indicators: Translate between domain objects and DTOs/ViewModels
May know about the web framework or ORM, but only at the boundary

layers.name: Frameworks and Drivers
layers.description: Outermost layer: databases, web frameworks, UI, external services. Details belong here.

criteria.name: Layer Separation
criteria.description: The degree to which the four Clean Architecture layers (Entities, Use Cases, Interface Adapters, Frameworks) are clearly separated in the codebase structure.

scores.0: No recognizable layer separation. Business logic, persistence, and presentation are mixed throughout.
scores.1: Basic separation present (e.g., MVC) but does not map to Clean Architecture layers. Major concerns are still mixed.
scores.2: Three or more distinct layers are identifiable (e.g., Entity, Service, Repository, Controller). Some cross-layer leakage.
scores.3: All four Clean Architecture layers are clearly separated, named, and consistently applied throughout the codebase.

criteria.name: Dependency Rule
criteria.description: Whether source code dependencies always point inward (inner layers do not import from outer layers).

scores.0: Dependencies point in all directions; inner layers import directly from outer layers (e.g., domain imports from ORM).
scores.1: Some effort to control dependencies, but inner layers still frequently import outer-layer specifics.
scores.2: Most dependencies point inward. A few violations exist (e.g., framework annotations on entities).
scores.3: All dependencies strictly point inward. Outer layers depend on interfaces defined by inner layers (Dependency Inversion Principle applied).

criteria.name: Entity Independence
criteria.description: Whether domain entities (business objects) are free from framework, ORM, and infrastructure dependencies.

scores.0: Entities extend or import from ORM/framework base classes. They cannot be instantiated without infrastructure.
scores.1: Entities have some framework annotations or utilities but could theoretically function without a running framework with effort.
scores.2: Entities are mostly plain objects. Minor framework dependencies (e.g., annotations for serialization) do not affect behaviour.
scores.3: Entities are pure domain objects with zero framework dependencies. They represent business concepts independently.

criteria.name: Use Case / Application Service Layer
criteria.description: Whether there is a clearly identifiable application service or use case layer that orchestrates domain logic independently of infrastructure.

scores.0: No use case or application service layer exists. All workflow logic is in controllers, models, or scripts.
scores.1: Some service classes exist but they mix application logic with framework or infrastructure concerns.
scores.2: Service/use case classes are present and reasonably separated, but some infrastructure coupling remains (e.g., direct ORM calls in services).
scores.3: A clear use case layer exists. Use cases are named after domain operations, are framework-free, and depend only on domain entities and repository interfaces.

criteria.name: Testability
criteria.description: Whether the core domain and application logic can be unit-tested in isolation, without requiring a database, web server, or other infrastructure.

scores.0: Unit testing domain logic is effectively impossible without a live database or running framework.
scores.1: Domain logic can be tested with significant mocking effort, but the architecture does not facilitate it.
scores.2: Domain and service logic can be unit-tested with moderate mocking. Repository interfaces or DI make isolation feasible.
scores.3: Domain logic can be easily tested in pure unit tests. DI, interface abstractions, and clean boundaries make mocking straightforward.

criteria.name: Abstraction and Interface Usage
criteria.description: Whether interfaces (ports) are defined for external dependencies (persistence, messaging, external services) allowing the Dependency Inversion Principle to be applied.

scores.0: No interfaces used for external dependencies. All code depends on concrete implementations.
scores.1: Some interfaces exist but are inconsistently applied. Most external dependencies are still concrete.
scores.2: Repository or service interfaces are used consistently for major external dependencies. Some concrete classes remain.
scores.3: All external dependencies are accessed through interfaces (ports). Concrete adapters are in the outermost layer. Full Dependency Inversion.

none.label: Does not follow Clean Architecture
none.description: The codebase shows no meaningful attempt to apply Clean Architecture principles. Layers are collapsed, dependencies are uncontrolled, and testing domain logic requires infrastructure.

partial.label: Partially follows Clean Architecture
partial.description: Some Clean Architecture elements are present (e.g., service layers, repository patterns), but the application does not consistently enforce the dependency rule or achieve entity independence.

mostly.label: Mostly follows Clean Architecture
mostly.description: Most Clean Architecture principles are applied. Clear layering, mostly inward-pointing dependencies, and good testability are present, but minor violations or framework coupling exist.

full.label: Fully follows Clean Architecture
full.description: The codebase demonstrates consistent application of all Clean Architecture principles: strict layer separation, the dependency rule, entity independence, clear use cases, excellent testability, and full use of abstractions.
